title: Setting Up Testing with Jasmine & Karma 🧪
description: Learn how Angular's test infrastructure works, configure Karma, and write your first Jasmine test.

slides.title: Why Testing Matters 🛡️
slides.content:
# Testing = Confidence

Testing ensures your application behaves as expected after every change. Angular was designed with testability in mind.

- Every component, service, directive, and pipe can be tested independently.
- Angular CLI scaffolds test files automatically (`.spec.ts`).
- Tests run with **Jasmine** (test framework) and **Karma** (test runner).
- A solid test suite catches bugs early, documents expected behaviour, and enables fearless refactoring.

slides.title: Jasmine: The Test Framework 📝
slides.content:
## Jasmine Basics

Jasmine provides the syntax to describe and assert code:

- `describe('component name', () => { ... })` – groups related tests.
- `it('should do something', () => { ... })` – a single test.
- `expect(actual).toBe(expected)` – an assertion.

Angular also provides `beforeEach` to set up the test environment before each spec runs.

quizData.question: Which function defines a single test case in Jasmine?
quizData.explanation: `it` is the Jasmine function for an individual spec (test).

slides.title: Karma: The Test Runner 🏃
slides.content:
Karma launches a browser (or headless Chrome) and executes your specs, reporting results in the terminal.

- Configured via `karma.conf.js` (in Angular project root).
- Watches for file changes and re‑runs tests automatically.
- Run with `ng test`.

Angular CLI sets up Karma with Jasmine and generates the configuration out of the box.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Headless Chrome for CI

In `karma.conf.js`, set `browsers: ['ChromeHeadless']` for faster, non‑UI test runs in your CI pipeline.

quizData.question: The Angular CLI command to launch tests is `ng _______`.
quizData.explanation: `ng test` builds the app and runs Karma.
